questions.question: For a life aged $x$, let $K_x$ be the integer number of completed future years. Its curtate expectation is $e_x=\mathbb{E}[K_x]$, assumed finite. Why need $e_x$ not be an integer?
options: Probability-weighted averaging can produce a fractional number.
Curtate lifetime includes the uncompleted fraction of the final year.
Current age is added to the completed-year count before averaging.
The final value is rounded up to include the year of death.

questions.question: A life has non-negative future lifetime $T_x$. Its $n$-year complete term expectation is $\mathbb{E}[\min(T_x,n)]$ for horizon $n>0$. What happens to an outcome with $T_x>n$ in this expectation?
options: It is removed before averaging over the remaining outcomes.
It contributes zero because death occurs outside the term.
It contributes its full duration because death is eventually certain.
It contributes duration n rather than its full lifetime.

questions.question: Let $T_x\ge0$ be future lifetime and $K_x=\lfloor T_x\rfloor$. Both have finite means $\mathring e_x$ and $e_x$, respectively. Which ordering follows without further assumptions?
A life has future lifetime $T_x\ge0$ and completed-year count $K_x=\lfloor T_x\rfloor$, with finite expectations. Why is $\mathbb{E}[T_x]-\mathbb{E}[K_x]$ at most one year?
options: Every outcome has at most one completed future year.
The expected total lifetime is rounded to the nearest year.
Every outcome discards a final fraction smaller than one year.
Survival after one further year has probability zero.

questions.question: A life has continuous future lifetime $T_x$ and curtate count $K_x=\lfloor T_x\rfloor$. Survival probabilities $\mathbb{P}(T_x>k)$ at years $k=1,2,3$ are 0.8, 0.6 and 0.4, and are zero from year 4 onward. What is $\mathbb{E}[K_x]$?
A life has future lifetime $T_x$ uniform on $(0,4)$ years, with survivor $\mathbb{P}(T_x>t)=1-t/4$ for $0\le t\le4$. What is its two-year complete term expectation $\mathbb{E}[\min(T_x,2)]$?

A life has continuous future lifetime $T_x$ and $K_x=\lfloor T_x\rfloor$. Survival to years 1, 2 and 3 has probabilities 0.9, 0.7 and 0.3. What is its two-year curtate term expectation $\mathbb{E}[\min(K_x,2)]$?
A life has non-negative future lifetime $T_x$ with infinite full mean. For a finite term horizon $n>0$, can complete term expectation $\mathbb{E}[\min(T_x,n)]$ still be finite?
options: Yes; the capped duration lies between zero and n.
No; capping cannot change the finiteness of a lifetime mean.
Yes; it equals n because the full mean is infinite.
No; infinite mean means the life cannot die at a finite time.

questions.question: A life has non-negative future lifetime $T_x$ with finite mean and complete term expectation $m(n)=\mathbb{E}[\min(T_x,n)]$. For horizons $0<n_1<n_2$, which condition is necessary and sufficient for $m(n_2)=m(n_1)$?

A life has continuous future lifetime $T_x\ge0$, survivor $p(t)=\mathbb{P}(T_x>t)$ and complete term expectation $m(n)=\mathbb{E}[\min(T_x,n)]$. For $n\ge0$, which expression equals $m(n+1)-m(n)$ for every such lifetime law?

A life has future lifetime $T_x$ uniform on $(0,2)$ years, with survivor $p(t)=1-t/2$ on $0\le t\le2$ and zero thereafter. What is its second moment $\mathbb{E}[T_x^2]=2\int_0^\infty t p(t)\,\mathrm{d}t$?
A life has future lifetime $T_x$ uniform on $(0.2,0.4)$ years and completed-year count $K_x=\lfloor T_x\rfloor$. What is the difference $\mathbb{E}[T_x]-\mathbb{E}[K_x]$?

A life has continuous future lifetime $T_x$ with survivor $\mathbb{P}(T_x>t)=2^{-t}$ for $t\ge0$. Let $K_x=\lfloor T_x\rfloor$. Which ordered pair gives complete mean $\mathbb{E}[T_x]$ and curtate mean $\mathbb{E}[K_x]$?
A life has future lifetime $T_x$ uniform on $(0.8,1.2)$ years and $K_x=\lfloor T_x\rfloor$. Which ordered pair is $\bigl(\mathbb{E}[K_x],\lfloor\mathbb{E}[T_x]\rfloor\bigr)$?
A life has non-negative future lifetime $T_x$ and $K_x=\lfloor T_x\rfloor$. Their means may be infinite. What does $K_x\le T_x<K_x+1$ imply about finiteness of the complete and curtate expectations?
options: Finite complete expectation implies finite curtate expectation only.
Each expectation is finite exactly when the other is finite.
Finite curtate expectation implies finite complete expectation only.
Neither expectation being finite restricts the other.

questions.question: Two currently alive lives have future lifetimes $T_A$ uniform on $(0,2)$ and $T_B$ uniform on $(0.5,1.5)$ years. Both have complete mean one. For horizon $n=3/4$ year, which pair gives $\mathbb{E}[\min(T_A,n)]$ and $\mathbb{E}[\min(T_B,n)]$?
A life has future lifetime $T_x$ uniform on $(1.8,2.2)$ years and $K_x=\lfloor T_x\rfloor$. With fractional horizon $n=1.5$ years, what is curtate term expectation $\mathbb{E}[\min(K_x,n)]$?
